question: Under which category of wetlands, are delta and mangrove swamps included?
solution:
Here the correct answer is **Estuarine.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Delta and mangrove swamps** are included under the category of **estuarine wetlands.**
 
• This is mentioned in the passage, where it is stated that the Cowardin et al., 1979 classification system categorizes wetlands into five types, which includes **estuarine wetlands comprising of deltas, tidal marshes, and mangrove swamps.**
 
• Let's have a look at the **fourth line **of the** first paragraph**:
 
 
• *One of the first widely used wetland classifications systems, devised by Cowardin et al., 1979, categorized wetlands into marine (coastal wetlands), **estuarine (including deltas, tidal marshes, and mangrove swamps),** lacustrine (lakes), riverine (along rivers and streams), and palustrine ( marshes, swamps and bogs) based on their hydrological, ecological and geological characteristics.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, **option 2) estuarine** is the correct answer.
